question_text: Find the centre, eccentricity, foci, length of the latus rectum and equations of the directrices of the hyperbola x² − 4y² = 4.

insider_note: All four results use only a, b and e, so get a² = 4 and b² = 1 right first — a mistake there breaks every one of the four marks, not just one.

steps.label: Write in standard form
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own — every result below reads a and b off this line.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by the number on the right so the equation reads = 1, then read a² off the x² term and b² off the y² term.
lines: The x² term is positive, so the transverse

lines.text: axis is the x-axis; a = 2, b = 1.

steps.why: The eccentricity, foci, directrices and latus rectum are all read off a² and b² once the equation is written in the standard form x²/a² − y²/b² = 1.
common_mistakes: Taking the coefficients 1 and 4 of x² − 4y² = 4 as a² and b² (a² = 1, b² = 4) without dividing through by 4 first.
Writing the standard form with a plus sign, as for an ellipse, instead of the minus sign a hyperbola needs.

steps.label: Eccentricity
steps.margin_note: First mark. a = 2, b = 1 from the standard form above.
steps.memory_tip: Hyperbola eccentricity ADDS a² and b² under the root — unlike an ellipse, which subtracts.
steps.why: For a hyperbola with the transverse axis along the x-axis, the eccentricity is the square root of a² + b², divided by a.
common_mistakes: Using a² − b² as for an ellipse instead of a² + b² — a hyperbola's eccentricity ADDS the two squares.
Leaving a² in the denominator (e = √(a² + b²)/a²) instead of a = √(a²).

steps.label: Foci
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The two 2's in a·e cancel, leaving just √5.
steps.memory_tip: Foci sit on the transverse axis (here the x-axis, since x² is positive), at distance ae from the centre.

lines.text: The foci are on the x-axis, a distance ae

steps.why: The foci of a hyperbola with a horizontal transverse axis lie on the x-axis, at distance ae from the centre on each side.
common_mistakes: Placing the foci on the y-axis instead of the x-axis.
Forgetting that the two 2's in a·e cancel, leaving just √5.

steps.label: Equations of the directrices
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Two separate vertical lines, one on each side of the centre.
steps.memory_tip: Foci use a·e (multiply); directrices use a/e (divide) — same pairing as an ellipse.

lines.text: The directrices are vertical lines, at a

steps.why: Each directrix is the vertical line x = a/e or x = −a/e — the reciprocal relation of the focus formula x = ±ae.
common_mistakes: Confusing the directrix formula x = a/e with the focus formula x = ae.
Leaving an irrational number in the denominator instead of clearing it.

steps.label: Length of the latus rectum
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. A short formula — do not overthink it.
steps.memory_tip: Latus rectum = 2b²/a (b² is the y² denominator, a is the semi-transverse axis) — the same shape as an ellipse's 2b²/a.

lines.text: The latus rectum is the chord through a focus,

steps.why: The latus rectum is the chord through a focus, perpendicular to the transverse axis; its length depends only on b² and a.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to double b² before dividing by a.
